facial-trauma.text: I found the clinical cases and practical aspects of panfacial trauma management most interesting, especially the diagnosis, fracture classification, and treatment approaches.

I found the various ways of assessing trauma the most relevant to my job, but enjoyed looking at the various cases, and outcomes.

Thank you for this excellent, clinically relevant course. It reinforced key principles in panfacial trauma management, particularly airway priorities and the sequencing of reconstruction. As a maxillofacial surgeon working in a conflict-affected setting, I found it highly valuable and would welcome further modules on trauma care in resource-limited environments.

The systematic approach to classifying and managing complex fractures, particularly the Le Fort fracture patterns and their clinical implications. aseptic-technique.text: I found learning about the chain of infection and how diseases spread most interesting. It helped me understand how to stay safe and prevent infections in real life.

I found the step-by-step explanation of the aseptic technique very interesting, especially the demonstrations of how to maintain sterility during different clinical procedures. The course was clear, practical, and easy to follow. I appreciated the focus on patient safety and the reminders about protecting key parts during procedures. Adding more hands-on examples or short demonstration videos in the future could make the learning experience even more valuable.

The practical aspects of aseptic technique, infection prevention, wound dressing, and identifying key parts and key sites. The course helped me understand how to prevent infection and maintain patient safety during clinical procedures.

anaesthesia-in-war.text: For anyone preparing for ICRC deployment or similar humanitarian missions, this course does not just teach what to do, it reshapes how you think about what anaesthesia is for.

This highlighted the need for context-specific approaches to trauma management.
The 5 pillars approach and damage control surgery. The content was very practical for conflict zones and helped me understand how to manage complex trauma with limited resources.
An excellent course, well presented, incredibly useful, lots of new info and ideas, from someone who's completed 16 ICRC field missions in surgery hospitals over decades. Thanks.

anaesthetic-considerations-vaginal-birth.text: I found the course particularly interesting in how it explained the anaesthetic management of vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC) in a clear and practical way. Learning how trauma teams prioritize resuscitation, pelvic stabilization, and hemorrhage control at the same time gave me a much better understanding of how quickly these injuries can become life-threatening.

The case-based discussions, imaging interpretation, and practical approach to pelvic fracture classification and acute management were the most engaging. They helped connect the theory to real clinical practice.

I found the sections on pelvic fracture classification and the correlation between radiographic landmark lines (iliopectineal, ilioischial) and the anatomical columns of the acetabulum particularly interesting. The case-based approach to hemodynamically unstable patients, especially the emphasis on the concurrent management of resuscitation, mechanical stabilization, and hemorrhage control, gave me a much clearer picture of how trauma protocols work in real clinical practice.

consideraciones-anestesicas-parto-vagina.text: Lo mejor de este curso es que explica de forma clara y práctica los riesgos, beneficios y el manejo anestésico del parto vaginal luego de cesárea, con tablas y guías útiles para la práctica clínica.

labour-epidural-analgesia-to-anaesthesia.text: I liked the part about continuous spinal anaesthesia.

cvad-complications-prevention-management.text: I found the modules on CVAD complications, infection prevention, and maintaining catheter patency particularly engaging. The practical focus on real-world scenarios, such as recognizing air embolism risks and managing occlusions, helped me connect theory to clinical practice. I also appreciated the clear explanations of colonisation routes and best-practice assessment strategies.

The videos were concise, engaging, and easy to follow, and I found the test yourself sections particularly helpful as they allowed me to check my understanding and confirm that I had grasped the key concepts.

Thank you for providing a well-structured and evidence-based course. The content was relevant, practical, and easy to follow. It has increased my confidence in preventing and managing CVAD complications and will support safe, high-quality patient care in my clinical practice.
I found learning about the different CVAD complications and how to prevent and manage them most interesting, especially infection prevention and maintaining catheter patency.
All the information was useful and practical and explained in a way that was efficient and will help me in my practice.
I loved learning about the complications and how they could all be simply prevented by the right skills and techniques.

difficult-airway-algorithm-2023.text: I love the swift pace of the course, it is great, and gave me a framework that, difficult airway algorithm hinges on the aspect of getting a difficult ventilation and intubation problem and attempting awake intubation is best so preparation is key in that sense and i get a refresher of LEMONS, MOANS, RODS and all, and i also liked how i get to be refreshed by the flowcharts.
Algorithm chart is very concise and understandable.
Well, I didn't know awake intubation was something in the hospital setting, I thought it was something for prehospital, and it makes a lot of sense using this approach for difficult airway.
The course provided clear explanations, practical examples, and useful clinical scenarios that helped me understand difficult airway management in a simple and interesting way.
The diagram showing me different types of oral openings and positioning, it made my understanding simpler.

difficult-caesarean-section.text: I liked the course as I am a scrub nurse in Maternity theatre. Even though I'm a scrub nurse this course helps me to anticipate my own actions and steps and help the surgeons to safely deliver while minimising risks. This bite size course is not heavy to even learn when in breaks on shift.
A well-structured and highly practical course. Thank you to the organizers and instructors for delivering such relevant clinical training.

drug-errors-anesthesia-2023.text: The clinical case scenarios were highly interesting and practical. They perfectly illustrated the different types of medication errors in anesthesia and how to prevent them.
The knowledge gained is approached in a practical way, making the content of the provided guide meaningful without relying on rote memorization.

ear-reconstruction.text: Showing real operating room cases was extremely helpful to understand the topic. Prof. showed different techniques in ear reconstruction.

I find more interesting the emphasis on early intervention, especially the use of ear molding in newborns within the first few weeks of life. It demonstrates the importance of timing in treating ear deformities without the need for invasive surgery.
It was a good experience for learning about the surgical procedure of ear.

ectopic-pregnancy.text: The most interesting aspect of this course was the detailed explanation of the pathophysiology and early diagnosis of ectopic pregnancy, especially the role of ultrasound imaging and quantitative beta-hCG monitoring. I really appreciated how the course highlighted early warning signs and danger signs, as well as decision-making regarding medical versus surgical management.

btk-ed-thoracotomy.text: The 'who' section gives a nice overview of the evidence.
The case scenarios were interesting and useful to understand the guidelines.

emergency-checklists-anesthesia-practice.text: I found the sections on cognitive aids in crisis management most interesting. Learning how symptom- versus diagnosis-based aids can guide clinical decisions during high-stress situations really highlighted the importance of structured support in patient safety. I also appreciated the practical strategies for implementing and customizing cognitive aids in the OR, including adapting them to local protocols and ensuring team-wide buy-in.

I found the discussion on simulation studies most interesting, especially how consistently cognitive aids improved team performance. I also really appreciated learning the difference between symptom-based and diagnosis-based aids, since that’s directly relevant to real-world crisis management.

I found the discussion on cognitive aids most interesting. Learning how symptom- versus diagnosis-based aids are used, and seeing how they improve performance in high-stress scenarios, was eye-opening. I also appreciated the practical examples from the operating room and emergency situations, which made it clear how these tools can directly impact patient safety.
The case studies were quite interesting due to the fact that it gives a realistic approach and response to the implementation of the cognitive aid.

The most interesting aspect of this course was learning how cognitive aids can effectively minimize human error and cognitive load during high-stress surgical crises. I also found the evidence-based strategies for improving team communication and the practical steps for implementing safety checklists in the operating room to be highly insightful.
The course was well organized, informative, and practical. It effectively highlighted the importance of cognitive aids in improving patient safety and team performance during critical events.

Thank you for providing this valuable course. The content was practical, clear, and highly relevant to anesthesia practice. I particularly appreciated the focus on patient safety and the use of cognitive aids during critical events.

epidemiology-fundamentals-patient-safety.text: What a great refresher course for me. I found all aspects of this course interesting. I particularly took notes while going through root cause analysis (RCA), and failure mode and effect analysis (FMEA). I absolutely love how they were both explained.

What I found most interesting in this epidemiology course is how it connects directly to real patient care and safety. Learning about things like near misses, adverse events, and the Swiss cheese model helped me understand that errors in healthcare are usually not just one person's mistake, but part of a bigger system issue. I also found it interesting how small breakdowns in the system line up and lead to serious outcomes.

I found the sections on patient safety, identifying medical errors, root-cause analysis, effective communication, and strategies for preventing errors most interesting. The real-life scenarios were particularly useful because they showed how system factors can contribute to errors and how they can be prevented.

The most interesting aspect of this course was learning how data and evidence can be used to understand real healthcare problems and improve patient care. I particularly enjoyed the parts about epidemiological data and patient safety because they showed me that even simple patterns in patient outcomes can reveal important issues that may otherwise be overlooked.

error-analysis-prevention-fundamentals-p.text: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Risk Priority Number (RPN) and Root Cause Analysis (RCA) are interesting to learn.

I found the sections on RCA and FMEA most interesting, especially learning how they can be used to identify underlying causes of errors and potential risks before they lead to patient harm. I also found the focus on improving systems and preventing future errors very valuable.
Very well rounded course! Delving into the FMEA model helped expand my understanding.

btk-esophageal-perforation.text: The lecture discussion was very useful and mimics a real scenario.
Thank you for the well conducted case based learning.
The flow of the scenario was seamless and clinically applicable across all settings. The major points were highlighted in Part B.
Discussion of real life scenarios is very useful.

essential-burn-care.text: The most interesting part of this course for me was learning how burn patients are assessed and managed from the first assessment until recovery. I found the topics about burn depth, total body surface area, fluid resuscitation, escharotomy, wound care, and early surgery especially interesting. I also learned that burn care is not only about treating the wound, but also about pain management, nutrition, positioning, infection prevention, and rehabilitation.

I found the assessment and management of burn injuries most interesting, especially the Rule of Palm, fluid resuscitation, escharotomy, wound dressing, and rehabilitation. I particularly found it useful to learn how early assessment and appropriate treatment can prevent complications and improve recovery.

I found the practical approach to burn assessment and the emphasis on multidisciplinary care most interesting. The focus on resource-limited settings was also valuable, as it highlighted that good burn care is possible even with limited resources.
I found the practical aspects of burn management, including fluid resuscitation, TBSA assessment, the Rule of Palm, and indications for escharotomy, most interesting and useful.
I have not considered the fact that there may be instances of late presentations of burn patients, especially in low income areas.

I particularly found the assessment of burn depth and total body surface area (TBSA), appropriate first aid, wound management, and indications for referral very useful. I also found the emphasis on cooling burns with cool running water for 20 minutes and avoiding harmful traditional practices particularly relevant to clinical practice.

essential-emergency-and-critical-care.text: The ABCDE approach, patient positioning (Recovery position, Semi-Fowler, Left uterine displacement) and the concept of 40 essential emergency and critical care processes were most interesting. The real-life case scenarios and practical low-cost interventions were very useful for students like me.
EECC in special groups, infants and maternity. In my practice, I rarely come across these categories. This course has helped me to gain confidence for when I come across them.

I found the assessment of critically ill patients most interesting, especially the ABCD approach, AVPU, and GCS. These topics were practical and helped me understand how to quickly assess a patient’s condition and identify signs of deterioration.

The practical approach, especially the ABCD method and EECC framework. I liked how simple, low-cost interventions can make a big difference. It changed my view that critical care isn't just about ICUs.
The modules on early recognition, airway management, and systematic triage stood out because they’re immediately applicable to real clinical situations.

The most interesting aspect of this course was learning about patient assessment, early recognition of critical illness, airway management, and emergency care. It improved my understanding of vital signs and the importance of timely intervention to ensure patient safety.

exploring-perioperative-nursing.text: I found the sections on burnout prevention and resilience strategies most interesting. The part about how empowerment and meaningful work reduce stress in the OR was very practical and new to me.

Understanding how structured communication like SBAR and TeamSTEPPS tools improves patient safety was also very valuable. Additionally, learning about infection prevention, aseptic technique, and OR efficiency and leadership practices helped me better understand how the surgical environment is organized to protect patients and ensure smooth operations.
I found the practical explanations and case-based scenarios very interesting. The course helped me understand surgical and patient care procedures better.

Thank you to the course creators and SURGhub for offering this valuable educational resource. The insights on patient advocacy and perioperative safety were extremely practical, and I look forward to applying these concepts directly to my daily practice in the operating room.
I have recommended this course to my friends because asides from being engaging, impactful, educational and all round interesting, I think it is something we can relate to as nurses.
The interactive components, quizzes throughout the modules. It reinforced the concepts of the lessons. The videos and scenarios was also added value.

facial-paralysis.text: I found the integration of anatomy, timing, and surgical decision-making in facial reanimation to be the most interesting part of the course. Understanding how lesion location and duration of denervation directly influence the choice between nerve repair, nerve transfer, or free muscle transfer gave me a clear, algorithmic framework for approaching patients with facial paralysis.

What I found most engaging was the interactive teaching style, which made complex concepts easy to understand with practical examples. Additionally, the content was well-structured, aligning perfectly with my skill development.

The most interesting aspects of this course were the practical clinical cases, facial nerve reconstruction techniques, and facial reanimation procedures. The explanations helped improve my understanding of treatment options and surgical decision-making.

fascia-iliaca-compartment-block.text: Applied anatomy, relevant to my clinical practice with rationale and clearly explained. I always find learning broad anatomy without clinical context very challenging.
Very helpful resources, I am doing the FIB under supervision. This online learning would really help me improve my knowledge and skills.
Information concise and organised in a way which makes it easy to understand.

btk-femoral-vessels.text: Excellent video and clear, concise teaching points.

fundamentals-war-surgery.text: The focus on trauma management, triage, and damage control surgery in combat settings, especially how surgical care is adapted to resource-limited and high-pressure environments.

Having completed the David Nott Foundation HEST-UK course, this course was a very useful add on, including more general background knowledge and an overview of humanitarian surgery principles beyond the operating theatre.

The practical application of concepts in real clinical scenarios, especially the structured approach to patient management and rehabilitation. The interactive case-based questions were also very helpful.

It was useful to understand the surgical aspects to war-injuries outside my own speciality of Neurosurgery, e.g., leaving wounds open and coming back in an iterative manner to carry out debridement. I also found the information around the legal background and ballistics interesting.

I found the systematic approach to trauma assessment, particularly the ABCDE approach, and the principles of emergency management in conflict settings most interesting. I also appreciated learning about wound management, bleeding control, infection prevention, and the importance of teamwork and clinical decision-making. These concepts are practical and relevant to my work as a nurse in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

This was an excellent and incredibly valuable course. I found all aspects highly interesting, especially the practical approach to burn management in low-resource settings, the assessment of inhalation injury, TBSA calculation, and the clear guidance on fluid resuscitation and surgical indications. Thank you for this wonderful course.

global-spinal-surgery-traumatic-spinopel.text: Excellent course! I appreciate the clarity of the presentation and the emphasis on practical clinical decision-making in trauma cases.

hand-trauma-reconstruction.text: As I'm a final year medical student, who is currently on internship rotations (exposed to hand surgery rotation with a massive amount of surgical procedures and cases). The most interesting part for me is the flap reconstruction and thumb replantation with microsurgery (I have assisted in a thumb replantation and took 5 hours to complete, but I didn't have much of knowledge as it was emergency case. After attending this course I'm confident with my knowledge).
Very good course in general. I knew most of the subjects but some tips were new to me in the management on tendon, nerve repair and flaps.
This is a great review of general concepts that help a surgeon identify and describe hand injuries.
I could find some points which are not mentioned in many textbooks as well as a slightly different (positively) approach to teaching and learning.
Overall, I found the course informative and clinically useful. I appreciated the practical focus and the opportunity to strengthen my understanding of hand and upper-extremity conditions.

I love the videos and the slow presentation of the modules. What I found most interesting was the applications of tissue flap reconstructive process and the application of nerve and vascular repair. Another useful point was the presenters experience of dealing with difficult traumatic injury that is quite common in practice. A more detailed follow up course or courses would be amazing.
The clinical cases, surgical techniques, and practical anatomy were particularly interesting and relevant to my daily practice as an orthopedic surgeon.

tecsalud-hand-washing-asepsis-desinfecti.text: I found the practical aspects of infection prevention most interesting, especially aseptic techniques, sterilization methods, hand hygiene, and the proper classification and handling of medical instruments. The real-world application of these practices to prevent infections and improve patient safety was particularly useful.

What I found most interesting: Hand washing technique. Realized 20 seconds plus all 5 moments isn't just a rule. That's literally where most infections get stopped before they start. Sterilization vs disinfection, the difference between killing everything including spores vs just reducing pathogens. How asepsis actually works in practice. Creating a sterile field sounds simple, but one touch breaks it. Shows how strict technique saves lives.

I found the topics on infection prevention, sterilization, hand hygiene, antiseptics, and safe handling of surgical instruments most interesting. They were practical and useful for maintaining patient safety in the operating room.

I found handwashing, asepsis, disinfection and sterilization the most interesting because I learned how each one plays an important role in preventing infection. I especially found it interesting to learn the differences between antisepsis, disinfection and sterilization and when each method should be used. These topics helped me understand how proper infection control can protect both patients and healthcare workers.
I find it most interesting when the lecturer talks about the different classification of sterilization and when and where can we use it.
Learning the differences in critical levels of the instruments. This kinda helped me with how I will now perceive my instruments.

head-neck-reconstruction.text: This course is very objective in explaining grafting in head and neck reconstruction. All the course was interesting and the cases helped a lot to improve my learning.
This course was very interesting, engaging, user friendly and most of all, it was very useful to me.

The practical clinical applications, reconstructive techniques, and management of complex head and neck surgical cases. The case-based content was especially useful and helped connect the concepts to real clinical practice.

crash-savers-trauma.text: The visual illustrations using YouTube videos and images to make every step clear was very helpful for me.
Foley catheter concept: it was new to me.
The aspect of this course that I find most interesting is the videos because they give a detailed illustration of how a procedure should be carried out.
All are good but especially I like the videos and it contains both amazing explanatory animations with real-life scenarios.

As a student midwife I have learned in my studies to manage PPH, postpartum hemorrhage, but during this I gained more information regarding different ways to stop bleeding in critical condition, all aspects were interesting but the most one was using Foley catheter.

infection-control-prevention-2023.text: The pre course quiz gave me a valuable insight over my knowledge of infection control and made me realise how much I had to learn. The course gave me a lot of information about HAI, their prevention and what mistakes we must never do as a doctor. The post course quiz helped me recall and answer.

I found the strict protocols regarding Propofol management and the emphasis on maximal sterile barrier precautions for central lines most interesting, as they highlight how critical anesthesia-specific timing and technique are in preventing hospital-acquired infections.

The prevention of hospital acquired infection, the importance of hand hygiene, the WHO surgical safety checklist and practical measures to prevent surgical site infection. The course was clear and practical for daily theater practice.
Made me realize that sometimes the most basic thing to do is the most important, like hand washing.

The hidden risks of PPE doffing: it was fascinating (and sobering) to learn that the vast majority of self-contamination occurs during the removal of PPE rather than the donning process. The emphasis on utilizing the buddy system and the strict mask on first, mask off last protocol provided a very practical solution to the risks we face during rapid OR turnovers.

Everything, it makes me think that I have to be more professional. I'm a PGY-2 General Surgery, sometimes here in Mexico, we don't take that much importance to hand-washing. Thank for this kind of courses.

I also found antimicrobial stewardship and the correct use of central lines and catheters very informative, especially how small practices like 'scrub the hub' and proper handwashing can significantly reduce hospital-acquired infections and improve patient safety.

I found the course very interesting because it explained practical infection control steps like hand hygiene, safe IV handling, and waste management in a simple and clear way. The short videos and real-life examples made it easy to understand and remember. I liked that it focused on safety for both patients and healthcare workers.
I was particularly surprised by how often self-contamination occurs during PPE removal and how critical it is to follow each step correctly.

Learning how healthcare-associated infections spread and how simple preventive measures can significantly reduce risks was very informative. As someone working in a medspa, I found this knowledge especially valuable for maintaining a safe environment for clients and professionals.

informed-consent-team-communication-cesa.text: I will like to give a thumbs up to the organizers of this program. It's taken me days to complete it but I will say it's worth it. I will like to add that I practically applied the concept of informed consent in an urgent CS I did over this weekend. It surely encouraged me to finish up the course. Thank you.

I found the real-life clinical scenarios and case-based questions most interesting, especially those involving informed consent during obstetric emergencies and situations involving cultural and communication barriers. The course helped me understand how to balance patient autonomy, cultural sensitivity, and the need for urgent medical care.
I found the scenarios on communication and consent in obstetrics emergency especially useful.
All contents are very useful for me, particularly the way how to take consent during urgent and emergency situation and the shared decision making approach.
Everything is interesting but what stood out more is the fact that most of the time, we don't consider that much the importance of family or community involvement in the consent.
This course is vital to us who are practicing in OBGYN, and I would like to thank the team who prepared this interesting and helpful modulary course.

interprofessional-communication-fundamen.text: The sections on communication, teamwork, and speaking up. The real-life scenarios showed how small communication gaps can affect patient safety and how simple tools like briefs, handoffs and time-outs can help prevent errors.
I found learning about authority gradients and communication interesting.
Very informative and helpful as it is concise.

I found the sections on communication, teamwork, authority gradients, and patient safety most interesting. I especially appreciated learning how tools like briefs, handoffs, time-outs, and debriefs can prevent miscommunication and reduce the risk of medical errors.

intervention-traumatologie-catastrophe.text: J'ai particulièrement apprécié la clarté des vidéos explicatives et les exemples qui illustrent bien les concepts théoriques.
En tant que infirmier au SAU le triage, les traumatismes, l’état de choc m’ont beaucoup intéressé.
Cette nouvelle approche est d'une grande importance dans la mesure où elle met l'accent sur le travail en équipe et en solidarité au profit du patient.
La partie que j'ai trouvé la plus intéressante c'est celle qui intéresse le management d'une équipe en traumatologie.

introduction-intraoperative-imaging.text: What I learn from this course to how to operate a C-arm machine with all safety protocol and most interesting part was how we can reduce dose.

I found the C-arm course very interesting because it gave me the opportunity to learn how to operate the machine correctly and safely. I was especially interested in learning about the proper positioning techniques and how to reduce radiation exposure. This knowledge is very important and useful for my future clinical practice.
I am confident to properly use our C-arm in the operating room.
Great general course to familiarize oneself with radiology safety. Does not focus on any specific system but rather can be applied to various settings and situations. Great course!

I found the radiation safety aspects of the course most interesting, especially learning about C-Arm positioning, dose reduction techniques, shielding, safe distance, and the importance of minimizing radiation exposure to both patients and staff.

I think it was well organized and easy to understand. I liked the photos included, especially the visual of the tape on the ground where the C-arm should be lined up if you have to pull it out and then go back in again.

musculoskeletal-tumour-surgery.text: I found the way in which surgical margins in sarcoma were explained (in the assessment section) very interesting.

The course was very thorough, systematic and exhaustive. It gave insights into a difficult and controversial though vital aspect of Orthopaedics. I would recommend this course to all Orthopaedic surgeons as it will add to their knowledge and help them in treating patients in a systematic manner.

The psychological aspect is what stands out to me the most. Engaging in sarcoma care in a resource-constrained setup, with multiple patients, often presenting with advanced disease, sometimes makes you forget the human aspect and pushes you to dissociate into a robot just focusing into the routine blunt jobs. So it is a nice wake up call.
The approach and the steps to take if a patient presents with musculoskeletal tumour, that really helped me.

Every aspect of it is perfect but more then all seeing real life patient interview after osteosarcoma successfully managed with multidisciplinary team is astonishing and amazing and also the mega prosthetic part that I see I envied you guys if we would have here in our country it is very much helpful.
The way the course connected pathology, radiology, staging systems, and treatment strategies helped me better understand the real-world approach to musculoskeletal oncology and patient management.

perioperative-management-spinal-cord-inj.text: The resuscitation and anesthetic consideration parts were highly interesting.

laparoscopic-cholecystectomy.text: The case based approach and the clear breakdowns of complex guidelines were excellent.
The structured breakdown of the critical view of safety and the step-by-step guidance on laparoscopic cholecystectomy technique were extremely clear and helpful.
Thanks, it helps me a lot to have a sound knowledge on basic laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
The video about techniques of cholecystectomy is very interesting and clear.

laparoscopic-handling-of-small-bowel.text: I really liked the templates and care the organizers took to help us build a low resource endotrainer; also I wouldn't have imagined I could use a bed sheet to simulate the small bowel and mesentery. I agree that management and handling of small bowel is a skill young surgeons don't feel too comfortable at the beginning and it must be thoroughly developed.
The guide on how to set up my own box trainer, that's very considerate especially for someone like me from Uganda who can't easily access one. Thank you so much team.
Case scenario is very interesting way to learn.

lavado-manos-asepsia-desinfeccion-esteri.text: Enfoque en la prevención de infecciones: el curso no solo te enseña a operar, sino que pone un énfasis crítico en la preparación previa (higiene de manos, clasificación de Spaulding), que es donde realmente se ganan o pierden las batallas contra las infecciones intrahospitalarias.
La forma de explicar de la ponente y las diapositivas 10/10.
Contenido claro, bien estructurado y muy aplicable a la práctica diaria. Los ejemplos de los 5 momentos de higiene de manos y la clasificación de Spaulding fueron muy útiles.

Los mejores aspectos del curso fueron la claridad de los contenidos, la información práctica y la facilidad para comprender los procedimientos y medidas de prevención. También considero positivo que los temas estén relacionados con situaciones reales del ámbito clínico, ya que permiten reforzar conocimientos importantes para la práctica profesional.

learning-and-teaching-ultrasound-guided-.text: The training changed how I view the transition from theory to clinical practice. Instead of attempting unfamiliar blocks after only reading about them, I now appreciate the value of following a progressive learning pathway that includes anatomy review, ultrasound scanning, simulation, supervised practice, and repeated performance until competence is achieved.

Overall, this was an excellent and highly structured course. Translating complex ultrasound physics into practical, safety-focused clinical habits is not easy, but this module succeeded beautifully. Thank you for putting together such a high-quality educational resource for regional anesthesia!
As a trainee, I found the practical approach to ultrasound-guided nerve blocks and the clear presentation of sonoanatomy extremely valuable for my daily clinical practice.
The elements of sonoanatomy was the most interesting. And how simply we were told to identify the main structure.

Learning why keeping the needle parallel to the probe + using a shallow angle makes it show up hyperechoic was really useful. The tip about practicing on meat/tofu phantoms before patients was also something I hadn't heard before.

The most interesting aspects of this course were learning ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia techniques, understanding sono-anatomy, and improving needle and nerve visualization. I also found the sections on patient safety, ergonomics, and recognition of local anesthetic systemic toxicity (LAST) very useful. The practical and step-by-step approach made the concepts easier to understand and apply in clinical practice.

Thank you for a well-structured and highly practical course. The step-by-step approach to UGRA ergonomics, safety protocols, and dynamic scanning techniques provided a strong foundation that will directly enhance patient safety and procedural accuracy in my clinical practice.

I found the practical ultrasound-guided regional anesthesia demonstrations and safety-focused teaching methods particularly interesting. The course explained anatomical landmarks, needle guidance techniques, toxicity prevention, and patient safety considerations in a very clear and clinically relevant way.

lip-cheek-reconstruction.text: The structured decision-making algorithms for flap selection, especially how reconstruction choices vary depending on defect size and location. I also appreciated learning the balance between achieving dynamic function and aesthetic symmetry, as well as the detailed case-based examples that showed how principles are applied in real clinical scenarios.

liste-controle-oms-chirurgie-sure.text: En tant qu'infirmière en chirurgie, l'entièreté du cours a été bénéfique pour mon apprentissage et l'évolution dans mes compétences professionnelles.

La vérification de l'accord du patient, la vérification de la disponibilité des médicaments et matériels anesthésiques, la préparation pour traiter toute complication. Tout cela préserve la sécurité du patient et m'intéresse beaucoup.
La vidéo de simulation en RDC sur la liste de contrôle de l'OMS. Très enrichissante.
Utilisation de la liste de contrôle OMS (vidéo), c'est vraiment la pratique réflexive sur la chirurgie sûre.

lumbar-plexus-block.text: The method of teaching was very easy to comprehend. Wonderful course.

managing-a-high-voltage-burn-in-a-low-re.text: Overall, the course was informative and useful. I particularly appreciated the practical focus on recognizing complications and making appropriate clinical decisions.

I appreciated the narration and the visual images. I think the course and the slides were well organized and I look forward to sharing this course for my colleagues to participate in too. I work onboard an expedition cruise vessel and we have engineers that work with high voltage equipment, so this information is very relevant to what we may encounter.
As a physiotherapist I work with burn rehabilitation patients. So, this course is very much useful for me.
It gave me a detailed but brief explanation on electrical burns. Anyone with the interests to learn can understand.

managing-pediatric-arm-contractures-in-a.text: The practical approach to managing pediatric arm contractures in low-resource settings, the case-based discussions, and the clear explanation of treatment principles were the most valuable aspects of the course.
I am a visual learner and the presentation contained the right amount of pictures and diagrams to help me engage and learn quicker.

manejo-basico-heridas.text: Son excelentes, ayudaron muchísimo a mi aprendizaje.

Los mejores aspectos del curso fueron el enfoque práctico, las explicaciones claras y basadas en evidencia, así como las recomendaciones para el manejo adecuado de heridas en diferentes escenarios clínicos.
Me gustó la disponibilidad del material en PDF y el video explicativo.

manejo-basico-quemaduras.text: Considero que los mejores aspectos del curso fueron que la información fue clara, práctica y fácil de comprender. Me gustó especialmente que se abordaran situaciones que pueden presentarse en la práctica clínica, como el manejo inicial de las quemaduras térmicas, químicas y eléctricas. También considero útiles los ejemplos y las evaluaciones, porque ayudan a reforzar lo aprendido.
La explicación de tipos de quemaduras estaba muy buena.
Me encantan los videos y los ejercicios.

medication-error-prevention-fundamentals.text: The real-life scenarios and strategies to prevent medication errors the most interesting. They show how small steps can directly improve patient safety.

The most interesting aspect of this course was learning about medication safety practices in anesthesia, including preventing medication errors, safe drug preparation, proper labeling, independent double-checks, and the importance of effective communication during patient handoffs.
This course made me realize that drug administration mistakes can happen at any second and that's why it is important to double check and follow all the safety rules.
The real-life case scenarios, practical medication safety strategies, and evidence-based approaches to preventing medication errors were the most interesting and useful.

Human factors and LASA errors: The ephedrine vs phenylephrine scenario stuck with me. Alphabetical storage plus look-alike vials equals perfect setup for a swap. I liked that the fix wasn't be more careful, it was separate the drugs in the cart. That's systems thinking.
The real-world case studies and examples of how medication errors occur. It was helpful to see the practical application of prevention strategies rather than just reading theory.
The course was clear, practical, and helpful for improving patient safety awareness.

microsurgery-workhorse-flaps.text: The knowledge, concepts, awareness, skills and relevance of all things which I have learned in this course were superb, I will use the information acquired in this course in my daily practice.
I like that the course included complex cases such as traumatic defects, cancer resections, and how microsurgical techniques and workhorse flaps can restore both function and form.

I actually recommended this video to people at work, especially to staff that closely work with reconstructive plastic surgeries. Very helpful for me as I deal with orthopaedic oncology cases that usually need reconstructive surgery.
Preparing to observe my first free flap case, very informative and I have a good idea of what to expect.

The most interesting aspects of this course were the practical microsurgical principles, the step-by-step approach to flap selection, and the discussion of workhorse flaps for complex reconstruction. I found it especially useful to understand how different flap options are chosen according to defect characteristics, vascular anatomy, and reconstructive goals.
Microsurgery principles, as I'm a general surgery resident I will use them at my practice.

nasal-reconstruction.text: The most interesting aspects of the nasal reconstruction course were the detailed breakdown of anatomical variations, the step-by-step explanation of techniques, and the practical surgical decision-making tips shared by the instructors. I particularly appreciated the focus on functional-aesthetic balance, graft selection, and complication management, which gave me a deeper and more structured understanding of modern approaches to nasal reconstruction.

The presentation was well detailed, and the diagrams eased my understanding of the concepts. The ladder system was well portrayed and I can't wait to practice it on the ground. This has made constructive surgery all interesting!

navigating-global-surgery-ecosystem.text: The courses focus on innovative surgical training, digital health and sustainable solutions for LMICs. The emphasis on local capacity building, collaboration, and using technology to improve access to surgical education and care was particularly valuable.
I would have to say the different perspectives and conversations from all over the world. It was an exceptional panel for the entire series and I'm leaving quite inspired.

This course felt less like a short training and more like a foundational diploma in global surgery. It answered many of the key questions someone new to the field might have, while also providing depth and direction for further learning. The quality of the curriculum design, the choice of panelists, moderation, and accompanying readings was exceptional. It gave me clarity, confidence, and a sense of belonging within the global surgery conversation.

I love the fact that this course easily brings out the global surgery burden, the underfinancing in the sector, the role of stakeholders in making policies that will allow the 33 million people that lack accessible surgical care to have a reach. It also speaks more to how LMIC can gain help through research and innovation, partnerships with local initiatives and the global organizations. It also speaks to me as a medical student on how to get involved in the global surgery movement, by first understanding the actual burden in my setting.

I’m really grateful for this program! It helped me see how my work in manufacturing surgical instruments directly fits into the bigger picture of global health. I'm excited to use what I've learned to help bridge the surgical gap in my region.

The way it connected the technical components of surgical care with the systems-level thinking required in global health. The discussions on how surgery functions as an essential health system intervention, rather than a specialty confined to tertiary hospitals, were particularly powerful. I was also very engaged by the sections on stakeholder mapping, especially understanding how clinicians, governments, nonprofits, academia, and industry all contribute distinct but interdependent roles in strengthening surgical systems.

nerve-stimulation.text: The sections on the physics of anesthesia (such as Coulomb's Law and nerve excitability curves) were highly engaging. I particularly enjoyed how theoretical physical laws were directly linked to clinical practice and nerve block procedures.
A good review for fresh starters as always.

nursing-care-in-war.text: The interactive case studies and the real-world applications of the theoretical concepts were the most captivating parts of the course. They made the material feel relevant and sparked my curiosity to explore the topics further.
Thank you for providing this course. The content was helpful and clinically relevant, especially for understanding wound assessment and management principles.

The most interesting aspects of the course were the practical approaches to patient safety, surgical teamwork, burn management, ballistic injuries, and radiation safety. I particularly found the focus on non-technical skills, communication, situational awareness, and decision-making useful because these factors can have a major impact on patient outcomes.

The communication tools module, especially ISBAR, TALK, and Closed-loop communication. Learning how to apply structured communication during handovers and emergencies was very practical and will directly improve patient safety in my daily work. The clinical nurse leadership part was also very inspiring.

The most interesting aspects of this course were the focus on nursing care in resource-limited and conflict-affected settings, as well as the emphasis on patient dignity, safety and adaptability. The modules related to wound care, patient assessment, CBRN/HAZMAT preparedness and nursing leadership were especially valuable because they combined practical clinical knowledge with humanitarian principles.

Found the practical, bedside-focused parts of the course the most interesting, especially: Systematic wound assessment (TIME model, tissue identification, exudate and edges), because it turns observation into a clear clinical decision. Linking theory to daily practice, such as choosing and applying dressings correctly rather than just knowing their names. Collaborative practice and communication tools (ISBAR, closed-loop, call-out), which show how patient safety depends as much on how we talk as what we do.

obstetric-trauma.text: The feedback and explanations after passing the post-course assessment was absolutely an amazing added benefit.

I really loved about trauma and physical injuries in general how they can affect the baby and mother, but before it affects them what I can do to save both of them. I loved the way this course is about saving life of two people.
The comparison of normal physiology of a pregnant vs a non pregnant adult is helpful to understand the contrast between the two, especially as a medical student.
The point about trauma and cardiac arrest during pregnancy, it's a golden part for me.

The most interesting aspects of this course were the physiological changes during pregnancy and how they affect trauma management, especially the interpretation of normal vs abnormal findings. The sections on placental abruption and its clinical signs were also very useful. In addition, the management of pregnant patients in hemorrhagic shock, including positioning to improve venous return and the decision-making around resuscitation and emergency delivery, was particularly relevant and practical.

I loved the theme. It's very heart breaking thinking on the worst but I was once on a situation that required preparation for the worst and I wasn't around, always had my thoughts on if I would perform a postmortem emergency cesarean delivery and the answer was yes. Now I've got certainty about what is the most correct way to perform. Thank you!

obstetrics-remote-retrieval-medicine.text: This course bridges clinical obstetrics with emergency medicine and transport logistics, which is rare. It forces learners to think beyond the hospital walls and consider how geography, infrastructure, and communication shape maternal outcomes.

The modules on postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) were especially powerful, not just for the protocols, but for the way they emphasized early recognition, teamwork, and the human impact of every decision. Learning about the role of tranexamic acid, the limitations of visual blood loss estimation, and the importance of reflex monitoring during magnesium therapy gave me tools I can use immediately in practice.
I appreciated the clear explanations, practical examples, and inclusion of evidence-based guidelines. Thank you for providing this valuable training; it will be very useful in professional practice.

The practical scenarios, illustrated by the cases, were interesting to read and learn from. It allowed the opportunity to reflect on practical scenarios that you have seen and managed at work and allowed me to form a strong association with the content. The layout on the content for the management of each case, in terms of predeparture management and management by retrieval team, was a useful approach and template to use and build on.
Very helpful information for learning, practical and relevant information about managing obstetrics and gynecological cases while in utmost remote health settings.

The most interesting aspects of this course were the practical approaches to managing obstetric emergencies, especially postpartum haemorrhage, pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, tocolysis, and patient positioning. I particularly appreciated the emphasis on early recognition, teamwork, patient safety, and evidence-based interventions that can reduce maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality.

oral-health-professionals.text: The quality pictures or visual aids used. It contained real live pictures of people with certain concepts being explained, I didn't need to search further to understand. The picture in the material showed me exactly the disease being spoken about. The pre course test as well was great. It piqued my interest before getting into the main course.
I enjoyed every aspect of it. It was a good revision tool for me.
Learning about different diseases that can be caused by clefts was interesting to me. There are a multitude of diseases and I loved hearing ways to help prevent them.
I found the lessons about cleft care, oral health, prevention, and teamwork among healthcare professionals most interesting.
The contributing factors to cleft were more than I was aware of and I do not have much experience with initial cleft treatment so aspects like managing scar tissues was also new information.

overview-of-skin-cancer.text: One of the most interesting aspects of this course was understanding the different types of skin cancer, and how their behavior, risk factors, and management differ. I found it especially valuable to learn how clinical features such as lesion size, borders, and location influence treatment decisions, including when to use standard excision versus Mohs micrographic surgery.

I found the clinical features most interesting. Learning how to spot different skin cancers by their appearance made it feel practical. The link between UV exposure and DNA damage also made the topic clear and logical. I also liked how each type behaves differently, which helps in real diagnosis.

pancreatic-cancer-surgery.text: The intense nature of the course I found very interesting and the appreciation of the required concepts were also of great interest to me. Now I better appreciate and understand the wide range of different types of pancreatic tumours and also the different clinical presentations and the principles of management of these tumours.

patient-centred-care.text: The clear presentation of real-world case studies was the most engaging aspect, as it made understanding the practical application of concepts much easier, along with the well-structured organization of the content.

The comparison between fee-for-service and value-based funding was most interesting. I liked learning how surgical safety checklists and better communication directly improve patient outcomes and reduce costs.

This course aligns well with the current global initiatives of improving access to quality healthcare. I am happy to have taken it at this early stage in my career. I will recommend all colleagues to pursue it.

Thank you for this excellent course. The content was clear, evidence-based, and highly relevant to clinical practice. I will continue to apply these principles and share them with healthcare staff through our person-centred care education activities.

I found the sections on PROMs, patient-centred care, shared decision-making, and value-based healthcare particularly interesting. The practical application of patient-reported outcomes to improve quality of care and support better clinical decisions was especially relevant to my work.

I found the discussion on how different payment and reimbursement models (such as fee-for-service, bundled payments, and value-based funding) influence clinical decision-making and patient-centred care particularly interesting. It gave me a clearer understanding of how financial incentives can shape provider behaviour, sometimes in ways that don't align with quality of care.

penetrating-thoracoabdominal-trauma.text: The course is very nice. I can say this is very good food for the health practitioner.
The simulation building is fascinating and possible even to construct at home and take to the residents or fellows at the hospital.
The videos were clear, and the material was beginner-learner friendly, I mean I am new to laparoscopy but things were flowing.

perioperative-blood-management-pediatric.text: It was short and precise, and there is a post test to check our understanding.

perioperative-medicine.text: I found the sections on perioperative risk assessment, frailty, functional status, prehabilitation, and the use of risk prediction tools such as P-POSSUM particularly interesting. I also found the discussion of identifying high-risk surgical patients and planning appropriate postoperative care very relevant to clinical practice.
The most interesting part was the aspect of prehabilitation and the statement to change the mindset of being on a waiting list for a surgery to preparing for a surgery.

I found the sections on preoperative assessment, risk stratification, frailty assessment, and prehabilitation particularly interesting. I learned how identifying comorbidities, assessing functional capacity, and optimizing nutritional status before surgery can help reduce complications and improve patient outcomes. I also appreciated the emphasis on multidisciplinary teamwork and patient-centred care.
The modules on perioperative assessment, risk stratification tools, and shared decision-making strategies were exceptionally structured, practical, and engaging.
I found the ERAS protocols and perioperative care guidelines most interesting. The practical examples and case studies were very helpful for improving patient outcomes.

pen-programme.text: I definitely enjoyed the leadership topic, and new topics for me were assertive communication, different types of waste and ways to improve Operating theatre production.

For me, every aspect of it was interesting because it elaborated my learnings here in the operating room. I get to be able to explain why is this happening, what should I prevent, what risks should I assess, everything of it helps me and knowledged me on how to give patient care effectively and safely.

Thank you for a really great course which was easy to navigate. I appreciate all of it. It was all very relevant to the operating room/surgical services setting. Thank you for all the hard work that went into putting together a very comprehensive, informative and research backed learning experience!
I found the sections on teamwork, communication, patient safety, and WHO surgical safety checklist most interesting. They were practical and directly relevant to my work in OR.

I find this course most interesting when we can learning about the perioperative patient journey and importance of patient safety. When we understand about preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative care work together to achieve of best outcome to patient safety and effectiveness of patient care.
The most interesting aspects of this course were learning how waste in healthcare affects efficiency and patient care, and seeing practical ways to create a productive operating theatre.

ppe.text: I found the infection control and PPE sections most interesting, especially learning the correct order for donning and doffing PPE and understanding how different types of protection work in real clinical settings. The content about N95 respirators, hand hygiene, and COVID-19 transmission was especially engaging because it directly relates to patient safety and real-world healthcare practice.

I found the infection prevention and control section most interesting, especially learning about different transmission routes (contact, droplet, airborne) and the correct use of PPE. It helped me understand how to protect both myself and clients in real-life situations.

I found the practical aspects of PPE use, infection prevention, and workplace safety most interesting. The course helped me understand how proper PPE selection and use protect both healthcare workers and patients, especially during anesthesia and surgical procedures.

I particularly enjoyed learning about the different types of PPE, when each should be used, and the correct way to put on and remove PPE safely. The practical aspects of infection prevention were especially useful because they can be directly applied in my daily nursing practice.

I found learning about infection prevention, proper PPE use, and the different routes of disease transmission most interesting. The practical guidance on hand hygiene, donning and doffing PPE, and safely reusing protective equipment was especially useful.

The material was presented in writing and in videos, which enhances consolidation, and unlike other modules where the learner is referred to YouTube for materials, in this module the videos are just a click. Thanks for the thoughtful preparation, thank you for contributing to saving lives in a safe way, Mwebalenyo (thank you).

postoperative-assessment-and-monitoring.text: The things that I found the most interesting were the way words were conveyed. Everything was explained in such a professional manner that also still helped you to understand exactly what was going on.
Undergoing training to be a PACU nurse, I found the whole course very interesting.
Learning about how to take proper care of patients postoperatively depending on their conditions.

I found the postoperative assessment and monitoring of patients most interesting, especially learning how to recognize early signs of complications and changes in the patient's condition. It helped me better understand the importance of timely assessment, proper monitoring, and prompt intervention to ensure patient safety and recovery.
I found the ABCDE part most interesting because nursing school emphasizes ABC and I forget about the DE part often.

access-epidural-space.text: Very helpful and informative course tutorial, really appreciate going through and answering the quiz questions.
Please keep on. Very informative course.
Epidural anesthesia is now on my finger tip, its technique and everything.

preoperative-assessment.text: Video tutorials very interesting and engaging.
Everything was informative, organised and explained thoroughly. Loved how concise the details were.

I found the preoperative assessment particularly interesting because it helped me better understand the importance of thoroughly assessing a patient's condition before surgery. I learned how proper assessment, identification of potential risks, and effective communication with the surgical team can help promote patient safety and prevent complications during and after the procedure.

pressure-sore-reconstruction.text: The interactive session and also the aspect of thinking about Marjolin's ulcer and the threshold for biopsy. Also, the aspect of autonomic dysreflexia was interesting too.
The different scenarios were interesting and helped me understand the concept of what I was learning a lot better.

regional-anaesthesia-children.text: The summaries on the differences in anatomy and pharmacokinetics were very useful to understand how to select and perform safe regional techniques.
The practical examples and clear explanation. The content was very useful and easy to understand.

I found the deep dive into the physiological and anatomical differences between pediatric and adult regional anesthesia highly interesting, particularly the specific rules regarding local anesthetic toxicity limits and the rationale behind using general anesthesia for pediatric blocks.

pen-program-spanish.text: Está super bien la forma de enseñar.
Todo muy bien interesante, muy bien explicado.

El curso es muy completo y aporta conocimientos prácticos que se pueden aplicar en el trabajo diario. Se valora el enfoque en ética, autonomía y consentimiento informado, ya que son temas fundamentales. Las evaluaciones ayudan a reforzar los contenidos, aunque algunas podrían ser más variadas para fomentar el pensamiento crítico.
Abarca muchísimos ámbitos y no solo la esfera del paciente y su cuidado, abarcan temas administrativos que son geniales.

self-learn-pulse-ox.text: Learning in depth exactly what the pulse oximeter does, its vital importance in diagnosis, and interpreting readings / measurements. This was excellent!

Thank you for this useful and well-structured course. The content was clinically relevant, clear, and applicable to daily anesthesia and perioperative monitoring practice. I appreciated the focus on patient safety, interpretation of pulse oximetry data, and recognition of situations where SpO2 readings may be unreliable.

I knew little to nothing about oxygen saturation and pressure exerted by oxygen before this course. I learned so much about pulse oximetry and I feel like I have a deeper understanding of hypoxia and how to use pulse oximetry to detect it.
The pulse oximetry course was in-depth and covered most scenarios that happen in a theatre environment.
The detailed checklist of what could be the reason for a patient to desaturate in the OT was very helpful.

I found the practical interpretation of SpO2 readings, the factors that can affect pulse oximetry accuracy, and its importance in early recognition of hypoxia and patient deterioration particularly interesting.

pulseoxcovidselflearning.text: It is practical and addresses what is found in the actual clinical areas.
The diagrams were captivating and clear to understand.
Learning has never been this fun. The inclusion of videos makes it more fun and helpful.

rapid-sequence-induction.text: Background on original Sellick paper and good coverage of drugs including doses.

I genuinely find that the demystification of RSI and the concise language used was most interesting of all, because intubation is scary, and RSI is even more, and this quick concise intro made it way more comfortable to learn the basics and practice.

The step-by-step breakdown of the RSI process was highly engaging, especially the emphasis on adapting the technique to different clinical scenarios. I also appreciated the inclusion of risks and complications such as bradycardia in children and awareness during induction.

The most interesting aspects were airway assessment, preoxygenation, drug selection, and the management of difficult airways and RSI complications. The course also improved my understanding of modern modifications to RSI and patient safety.

I found the entire course a wonderful review, and provided me with new knowledge that was never taught in my original ACP program. We were also never taught about using atropine as an anti-sialagogue when using Ketamine, which makes total sense.
I found the focus on airway safety and the step-by-step RSI technique most interesting. It felt very practical and directly applicable.

rectal-cancer-surgery.text: The method of teaching and demonstration of principles were found most interesting and the sequential nature of the modules has helped me to appreciate the following: 1. principles of rectal polyp surveillance, the principles and guidelines for rectal cancer follow-up, evidence for blood tests and imaging review together with the review of evidence for endoscopic surveillance. And 2. The aspect on the future treatments for rectal cancer, including understanding of the evidence and role of future treatments.
The clinical case discussions and integration of imaging with surgical decision-making were especially engaging.

canecsa-research-methodology-course.text: For me, the most interesting aspects of this course were the parts that showed how research connects directly to patient care. I found it eye-opening that the main purpose of clinical research is not just to publish papers but to actually improve outcomes for patients. Another highlight was learning about planning and structuring research questions.

Overall, the course was informative, well structured, and valuable for my anaesthesiology training. It has improved my understanding of clinical research and will be helpful in planning future research projects.

I found the modules on study design, data collection, and how to critically read research papers the most interesting. They are very practical and directly useful for quality improvement projects in the operating room.

I found the real-world examples most interesting, especially the CRASH-2 trial, which showed how a large randomised trial can change international guidelines. I also enjoyed learning how simple clinical audits, like the iron deficiency anaemia and bedside television studies, can answer practical questions without needing complex resources.

I found the sections on critical appraisal of papers and the practical sessions on literature searching the most interesting. Learning how to turn a research idea into a clear research question, and then choose a suitable study design, made the whole research process feel much more manageable.

The most interesting aspects of this course were learning about research methodology and understanding how to design meaningful research studies. I especially found the guidance on developing research proposals and approaching funding institutions valuable, as it provided insight into how research ideas can be transformed into practical projects. This knowledge will help me in planning future research and seeking opportunities to support evidence-based healthcare initiatives.

rural-urology-practice.text: The course was informative and well-structured. I appreciate the effort put into delivering relevant clinical content, especially topics like urosepsis, urethral trauma, and emergency urology care. It would be even more beneficial if future sessions included more hands-on demonstrations or virtual simulations to enhance understanding. Thank you for a valuable learning experience.
Even though I'm working in a tertiary hospital in my country, I can still find many similarities in the approach of patients, treatment plan etc.
This has really upskilled my surgical career. Thank you so much to Dr Jesudian.

handover.text: The real life examples shown in the video helped me a lot in realising the ISBAR3 method clearly.
The ISBAR use in most of our hospitals in South Sudan isn't being applied. Therefore, I have an advantage to have acquired more knowledge in effective communication.
I really loved the scenarios part, I understand why they put ISBAR3.
The scenario was the most interesting part for me because it was realistic, simple, and clear. It helped me better understand the situation, clarify the information, and organize my knowledge.
The way you guys showed the ISBAR3 through real-life clinical situation was truly interesting.

The most interesting aspect of this course was learning how structured communication tools can actively override human error during high-stress transitions. It was fascinating to see how easily critical data evaporates due to environmental distractions, exhaustion, and fragmented systems. Exploring the psychological and systemic vulnerabilities of clinical handovers highlighted that safety isn't just about individual diligence.

safety-culture-fundamentals-patient-safe.text: I found the most interesting aspects of the course to be the focus on patient safety culture, understanding the root causes of errors, learning about the Swiss Cheese Model, and seeing how effective communication and teamwork can prevent medical errors and improve patient outcomes.

I found the concepts of safety culture and just culture most interesting, especially the focus on system factors rather than blaming individuals. The discussion of open communication, leadership commitment, near-miss reporting, and learning from errors was very relevant to perioperative care and teamwork.

I found the focus on safety culture, open communication, and learning from near-misses most interesting. It highlighted how every healthcare professional, including radiographers, can contribute to improving patient and staff safety.
The case studies analyzing the breakdown of safety culture and the clear distinction between a just culture and a blameless culture were highly engaging and practical.

I loved that I got to answer questions and there were scenarios, because you never know what will happen so you have to be prepared for every possible case and you have to be careful and know what to do for the patient's safety and the team's safety.
The real-life clinical scenarios and patient safety cases were the most interesting because they felt realistic and applicable to actual practice.

scalp-reconstruction.text: Great course on scalp reconstruction, the MCQs and explanation were very helpful.
I found the quiz aspect fun and engaging and thought it useful to do the questions prior to the lectures to stimulate engagement.

Will be very grateful to have more of these similar free online courses for reconstruction of other regions of the body. This really highlighted the important principles to always apply in my practice.

I found the reconstructive algorithm for scalp defects most interesting, particularly how defect size, pericranium status, and tissue quality guide the choice between primary closure, local flaps, skin grafts, and free tissue transfer. The case based discussions and anatomy review were especially practical.
The course perfectly covered the issues about scalp reconstruction. It was useful to see real patient photos to understand the procedures.

soins-fondamentaux-brulologie.text: Personnellement, j'ai grave été instruit par tous les chapitres, étant un tout nouveau médecin sorti de la fac, ce cours m'a encore aidé à renforcer mes connaissances, certains aspects sont intéressants notamment la prise en charge des brûlures, l'évaluation primaire.

Les aspects les plus intéressants étaient l'apprentissage des différents types de brûlures, les premiers soins à administrer aux patients brûlés et les méthodes de prévention des infections. J'ai aussi trouvé très utile la partie sur l'évaluation de la gravité des brûlures.
C'est le cours en général, mais les aspects les plus intéressants, c'est sa pertinence dans le monde et plus particulièrement en Afrique, par exemple le cas de la RCA.
Le cours a bien fait le tour sur l'essentiel de la prise en charge dès la prévention primaire jusqu'à la réadaptation du patient.

speaking-up-operating-room.text: The properly simplified version of such an important but overlooked topic is most interesting for me. As I work in a perioperative department, this course is very helpful and easier to navigate for information.

I never realized how important speaking up in the operating room was until I took this course. I found it interesting to learn how communication tools like PACE can help team members raise safety concerns clearly and prevent patient harm. I also learned that everyone in the OR, regardless of position or experience, has a responsibility to speak up for patient safety.
It facilitates creation of a smooth environment for communication to avoid medical error.
I found the topic of speaking up in the OR and knowing when to escalate a concern the most interesting. The importance to speak up in a polite and respectful way.

spinal-anaesthesia-theory-and-practice.text: I found the procedure of spinal anaesthesia, its indications, contraindications, technique, and potential complications most interesting. The course helped me better understand its clinical applications and importance in patient safety.

The most interesting aspect of this course was learning about the practical application of spinal anaesthesia in different clinical scenarios. I particularly enjoyed learning about patient positioning, assessment of block height, drug selection and dosing, and the recognition and management of complications such as hypotension, high spinal block, and post-dural puncture headache.
The detailed aspect of the anatomy, physiology and pharmacology with respect to spinal anaesthesia made it very lively and approachable.
I found the practical approach to spinal anaesthesia, patient safety, and the management of complications most interesting and informative.

The most interesting aspect of this course was learning about the practical management of spinal anaesthesia, including patient assessment, prevention and treatment of complications, and the importance of effective monitoring during the perioperative period. The case-based scenarios were particularly valuable because they helped connect theoretical knowledge with real clinical situations.
I found assessing block height, understanding baricity and positioning, and managing complications such as hypotension and bradycardia most interesting.

implementing-reliable-systems-fundamenta.text: I learned a lot and enjoyed a lot too.

I found the sections on patient safety, identifying root causes of errors, and the influence of artificial intelligence in healthcare most interesting. I especially liked learning how system design, communication, and safety strategies can help prevent errors rather than simply blaming individuals.

surgical-foundations.text: Specifically, the sections on Pediatric Surgery (Module 31) and Neurosurgery (Module 34) provided very insightful foundations that are often hard to find in general introductory courses.

All aspects of this course were very interesting to me, honestly. But, the aspects of the Thoracic and Vascular Surgeries were in their own level for me and that maybe because of my special innate passion.

Many many thanks for this lovely course to SURGhub and COSECSA. It covered all the components of modern surgery, including recent research updates, virtual and illustrated pictures and videos of surgical procedures. Journey to learn surgery is starting from this special and basic course. Once again heartiest thanks SURGhub and COSECSA.
The pre-tests assessed my existing knowledge before starting the course, helping me identify areas I needed to focus on and revise.

I found the clinical case-based approach most interesting, particularly how the course connected common presentations with diagnosis, staging, and management of urologic cancers. The sections on RCC, bladder cancer, prostate cancer, testicular cancer, and penile cancer were especially useful because they highlighted important risk factors, patterns of metastasis, and practical treatment decisions.

surgical-instrument-testing-and-inspecti.text: I found the sections on visual inspection and functional testing of surgical instruments the most interesting, especially learning how to identify defects, check alignment, tension, and movement. These practical, real-world examples helped me better understand how proper inspection improves patient safety and the reliability of surgical procedures.

I found the most interesting aspects of this course to be the practical approach to inspecting and testing surgical instruments. The detailed explanation of visual inspection and functional testing, especially sharpness, alignment, and tension testing, was very valuable. I also found it interesting how proper inspection can directly impact patient safety and improve surgical outcomes.

One of the most engaging parts is learning inspection criteria and defect recognition. This includes identifying issues like micro-cracks, corrosion, misalignment, dull cutting edges, and surface pitting. These details matter because even tiny defects can affect surgical outcomes or cause instrument failure in the operating room.
Thanks for the module, as surgical intern, these are the tutorials for me to teach the theater assistants at our facility.
Learn more about the handling of surgical instruments from a perspective that we as physicians sometimes take for granted but that is very important for the proper recovery of our patients.

I found the practical, hands-on guidelines for surgical instrument inspection and sharpness testing the most valuable. Learning the specific testing protocols for different specialty instruments (like using index cards for Kerrison rongeurs versus plastic dowels for osteotomes) provided clear, real-world context for sterile processing standards.

tecsalud-suture-technique.text: First, the detailed explanation of different types of sutures, including absorbable and non-absorbable materials, helped me understand their specific indications and appropriate uses. The step-by-step demonstration of various suturing techniques, such as interrupted, continuous, and intradermal stitches, was very helpful in visualizing the practical application.
I found the different types of sutures and their uses the most interesting. I also liked learning how to choose the right suture for different types of wounds.
Covering the suture details, most of us just use the suture without knowing the details, just following our colleagues. A good insight into suture profiles is very much appreciated.
I liked seeing the different kind of suture techniques and seeing the videos of each one.

I found the hands-on demonstration of proper needle handling and wrist technique most interesting. Seeing the correct entry angle, spacing, and tension made the mechanics of suturing much clearer than just reading about it.
