I also appreciated the discussion on tissue handling and how proper technique directly impacts wound healing and patient outcomes.
I really appreciated how the course was set out as it was very direct and informative. I have done other suturing reviews and this was a nice compilation of them.

I found the section on suture materials and selection most interesting. Understanding the difference between absorbable sutures like Vicryl and non-absorbable sutures like Nylon and Prolene, and when to use monofilament vs multifilament, was very practical and will help me in my daily practice.

btk-suturing-horizontal-mattress.text: I practiced independently while the video was playing, which made the experience very engaging.
Very very good presentation. Please add virtually practicing surgical games like app.
Learned the mattress technique which will help polish my suturing.

I found the practical aspects of the course most interesting, particularly learning different surgical techniques and understanding when and how to apply them in clinical situations. The hands-on and practical information made the course engaging and useful.

btk-suturing-vertical-mattress.text: I really enjoyed the video most because it was very hands on. I felt like I could do it myself.
The course was productive and really interesting, have learnt a lot.
The video demonstration, it put such a complex process to an understandable lesson.
The explanation was clear and loved the change of view with the camera for a better understanding of the technique.
I found the vertical mattress suturing technique most interesting, particularly how the far-far, near-near method helps close wounds under tension and properly evert the wound edges.

tecnica-suturas-puntos.text: Me encantó que en muy poco tiempo, pudiera aprender tanto, ya que por mis tiempos entre el trabajo y el hospital, no cuento con mucho y esta forma de enseñanza, es bastante práctica.
El hecho que no solo explica la técnica de sutura, sino que nos da a conocer el por qué, para qué sirve, en qué no funciona y aprender cómo checar cuál es el más conveniente para mi paciente.
Claridad en la toma de decisiones: te ayuda a diferenciar conceptos clave como capilaridad, absorción y fuerza tensil, que son vitales para evitar complicaciones como dehiscencias o abscesos.
La explicación clara y concisa del contenido, junto con los videos donde se ve la realización de los 3 puntos de sutura expuestos (simple, de colchonero o Sarnoff e intradérmico).
Definitivamente el cómo se te explican los diferentes tipos de sutura, junto con los ejemplos y sobre todo las preguntas que ayudan a retroalimentar lo que vi y aprendí.

Considero que los mejores aspectos del curso fueron el enfoque práctico y la explicación de diferentes técnicas de sutura aplicables a situaciones clínicas reales. También me pareció útil que se abordaran aspectos como la selección de la técnica, el manejo adecuado de las heridas y la prevención de complicaciones. Los ejemplos y demostraciones facilitaron la comprensión y ayudaron a relacionar la teoría con la práctica clínica.

labour-epidural-troubleshooting.text: Everything, it is not very often that you get to train properly on epidural management at the hospital, as anesthesiologists (at least in my country of formation) don't like sharing their knowledge with anyone other than their own residents, so I really appreciate this opportunity for learning! Did learn a lot!!
This program is the best and helping, especially it has helped me a lot.
Thinking on the different options on why epidurals fail, considering migration as an important factor. The clinical cases were fantastic.

tranexamic-acid.text: The most interesting aspect of this online course was learning about tranexamic acid, especially its mechanism of action in controlling bleeding and its wide range of clinical applications such as trauma, surgery, and obstetric hemorrhage. I also found it valuable to understand when it should and should not be used in different clinical situations.
It has been great taking this course. It refreshed my knowledge about the use of TXA.
Cały temat był interesujący i przydatny w pracy ratownika medycznego.

It provided a clear understanding of the clinical applications of tranexamic acid in trauma, peri-operative care, obstetrics, orthopaedics, and critical care settings. The most engaging aspects were: the mechanism of action of tranexamic acid and its role in fibrinolysis; evidence from major clinical trials in trauma and post-partum haemorrhage; practical dosing protocols and safety considerations; its expanding applications in surgery and emergency medicine.

The fact that tranexamic acid has anti-inflammatory effects and reduces the SIRS was nice to know. Also, since it is safe for breastfeeding, if there is PPH after delivery of the baby, I could prescribe it to those mothers.
All the course was relevant. I mostly enjoyed knowing the different uses of TXA and the side effects of that product as well.

transversus-abdominis-plane-block.text: Learning the anatomy of the abdominal wall and the nerve innervation makes it easy to grasp the concept of why we use the blocks and how to adequately perform them.
Please, I'm grateful that I've learnt the skills of giving TAP block.
Improve skills and knowledge in regional anaesthesia.
Thanks a lot for improving my knowledge easily, with also a certificate that increases my CV strength.

trauma-disaster-team-response-mcgill.text: I found the trauma assessment, triage, and emergency management topics most interesting. I especially liked learning how the ABCDE approach helps nurses quickly identify life-threatening problems and how START and JumpSTART are used during disasters. I also found the different roles within the trauma team interesting because it showed me how important communication and teamwork are for providing safe and effective patient care.

Thank you for providing a well-structured and informative course. The practical trauma scenarios and case-based learning were particularly valuable. The content was relevant, easy to follow, and applicable to real clinical situations. I appreciate the effort of the instructors and course developers and look forward to participating in future training programs.

The most interesting aspects were the practical trauma approach, especially the primary survey, airway management, shock recognition, chest trauma, pediatric trauma, pregnancy trauma, burns, and START/JumpSTART triage. I found the case-based questions helpful because they connected the lectures to real emergency decision-making.

What I found most interesting was how the course combined clinical reasoning, rapid decision-making, and team coordination. The simulation scenarios really highlighted how small changes in communication or prioritization can dramatically affect patient outcomes.

I found the topics about trauma assessment, burn management, pain control, and START triage the most interesting. I especially liked learning how to quickly assess patients, identify life-threatening problems, and decide which patients need urgent treatment.

The most interesting part of this course was learning how to manage chaos through teamwork rather than just surgical skills. It completely changed my perspective by showing how communication failures can cause more damage during a crisis than a shortage of medical supplies.

triage-resuscitation.text: The strict logic of the START algorithm is fascinating because it forces a complete shift in standard clinical thinking.

I found the practical differences between adult and pediatric trauma care most interesting, especially how children can deteriorate quickly because of their smaller blood volume, faster heat loss, and different airway anatomy. I also found the airway section useful, such as using bag-mask ventilation carefully, placing an NG tube if the stomach becomes distended, confirming intubation with end-tidal CO₂, and being careful with the fragile palate.

I found the practical and clinically relevant aspects of the course most interesting, particularly the focus on patient assessment, recognizing deterioration, prioritizing care, and making safe clinical decisions. The examples were especially useful in improving my confidence and applying the knowledge to clinical practice.

The most interesting part of the triage course was learning how to prioritise patients based on the severity of their condition and applying triage principles through practical scenarios. It helped me better understand rapid assessment and decision-making in emergency situations.
Excellent refresher on emergency triage and primary trauma assessment protocols. The rationales provided for incorrect options were particularly helpful for reinforcing clinical reasoning.

I found the practical approach to trauma assessment and management most interesting, especially the clear prioritization during triage and the step-by-step handling of critical situations like airway compromise and shock.

trocar-placement.text: Port placement techniques, and I really like the open technique.

arterial-blood-pressure-measurement.text: I am a nursing student, and I never knew that ABP can be measured and as well it's more accurate. Thanks.
Reinforced my knowledge of what the waveform related to in the different parts of the cycle.
Damping, Allen test, zeroing are well explained plus visual representation is also very informative.
I found the practical knowledge, clinical skills, and real-life scenarios most interesting because they will help me improve my skills and provide better patient care.
All the information was relative and informative and has helped me refresh my knowledge on arterial blood pressure monitoring.
I found the arterial line monitoring, waveform interpretation, and troubleshooting most interesting.

understanding-capnography.text: I enjoyed all of the course and it was easy to follow as a paramedic science student :)
The bite size information, the content is engaging and very interesting.
All aspects are interesting because it reflects in my daily clinical work in operating room.

I found the interpretation of the capnography waveform most interesting, especially how changes in the EtCO₂ and waveform can help assess ventilation, detect airway problems, and recognize changes during CPR and anesthesia.
I really enjoyed the information regarding the different abnormal tracings.

local-anaesthetic-systemic-toxicity.text: I found the sections on early recognition of CNS excitation and the mechanism of Intralipid therapy particularly interesting. The real-world case examples helped tie everything together.
I liked the format of each slide being a question and the content of the slide being an answer.
The focus on early recognition of LAST signs was particularly valuable. Understanding subtle clinical indicators and how to differentiate them from other complications was extremely insightful.

What I found most interesting was how knowledgeable I became about LAST in such a short amount of time. I finished understanding the early warning signs, progression of toxicity, the risk factors and importance of rapid treatment with lipid emulsions.
I enjoyed learning about the use of Intralipid and the role (or lack of role) of Propofol in the management of LAST.

heat-stable-carbetocin-for-prevention-of.text: I found the information about heat-stable carbetocin, its long-lasting effect, and its role in preventing PPH most interesting. The practical guidance on administration and contraindications was especially useful.
I'm sincerely grateful for the opportunity to learn and improve my knowledge on prevention of primary PPH due to uterine atony.

Informative but very visual and simple to understand. Engaging course despite not having any videos. Love that there is assessment at the end of every lesson to refresh and help retaining information learnt.

The information about heat-stable carbetocin, its advantages over oxytocin regarding storage without cold chain, its long-acting nature, single dose administration and its role in PPH prevention was most interesting and very relevant to my clinical practice.

I found the practical administration guidelines and the clear distinctions between oxytocin and heat-stable carbetocin most interesting. The contraindications and correct dosing information were particularly useful for clinical application.

I liked the fact that the course just didn't stop at telling me there's a latest discovery to be incorporated. It went ahead to do justice with the composition, characteristics, why it is preferred and how to effectively use and safeguard it.

vascular-malformations.text: I found the detailed explanation of the different types of vascular malformations, capillary, venous, lymphatic, arteriovenous, and mixed, particularly interesting. The discussion of their clinical presentations, associated complications, and the Schobinger staging system for AVMs was especially valuable. I also appreciated the practical surgical cases, including preoperative evaluation, debulking techniques, and postoperative management. These real examples made the content clear, applicable, and clinically relevant.
I found all the aspects of the course very interesting.
Very informative indication of surgical treatment of VM.
Clear and systematically mapped out overview.

video-consultations.text: I enjoyed how clear the narrator's voice was, it made it easy to follow along. I also loved the illustrations which helped break the monotony. I am also a fan of the research papers and other additional content provided.
Scenarios were fantastic in demonstrating positive and negative aspects of video consultations.
More courses like this would be great.
The references for telehealth communication are very useful.

z-plasty.text: I find the simulations interesting, providing great visualization and better understanding.

I found the precision and technique involved in Z-plasty, particularly in altering scar direction and improving functional and aesthetic outcomes, most interesting. The way small adjustments in angles can significantly impact scar healing and appearance was fascinating.

The most interesting part was how Z-plasty design directly changes scar behavior. Seeing how adjusting limb angles (like 30 to 60 degrees) and lengths actually affects tension, lengthening, and final scar orientation made it feel very practical, not just theory.
The surgical simulation that allows you to apply the knowledge acquired is a great tool.
The interactivity was a great feature. Much thought was put into this course, and it is apparent. The DIY kit was also an amazing touch making it much more engaging and fun.
An excellent, practical course that strongly reinforces surgical principles through simulation.

I had heard of the term Z-plasty before and knew it was used in lip reconstruction and pilonidal sinus but never thought about the specific angles to increase length etc. It was super cool to know. Also the model for physical simulation was really cool and easy to make.
The most interesting part is the simulation that lets us understand more of how to measure the flap.
